'''Jens Marklof''' is a German mathematician working in the areas of [[quantum chaos]], [[dynamical systems]], [[equidistribution]], [[modular form]]s and [[number theory]].<ref name="JMHP">{{cite web|url=http://www.maths.bris.ac.uk/~majm|title=Jens Marklof's Homepage|author=Jens Marklof}}</ref><ref name="UoB">{{cite web|url=http://www.maths.bris.ac.uk/people/faculty/majm/|title=Prof Jens Marklof|author=University of Bristol}}</ref> He will be president of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in the period 2023-2024.

Marklof is currently professor of mathematical physics at the [[University of Bristol]], UK.<ref name="JMHP" /><ref name="UoB" />

==Education==
After studying physics at the [[University of Hamburg]], Marklof was awarded a doctorate in 1997 at the [[University of Ulm]].<ref>{{cite web | title =Jens Marklof, University of Bristol, UK - Biography | work =Complex patterns in wave functions - drums, graphs, and disorder | publisher =The Royal Society | year =2012 | url =http://royalsociety.org/events/2012/complex-wave/ | accessdate =21 June 2012 }}</ref>

== Awards and honours==
In June 2010, Marklof was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]] for his work on quantum chaos, [[random matrices]] and number theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/About_Us/news/2010-06%20LMS%20Prizes%20(2%20July).pdf |title=Prize Winners 2010 |author=London Mathematical Society }}</ref> Marklof was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2015|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2015]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jens-marklof-11900/|title=Jens Marklof - Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org}}</ref>
